name: splats
description: A free collection of objects as 3D Gaussian splats, made three ways: generated by an AI model from a single freely-licensed photograph, converted directly from classic meshes at four resolutions, and scanned from phone video. Each object is labelled with how it was made and what license it carries.
license: per object (see each record's license field)
license_note: The collection has no single license. Scanned objects are CC-BY-4.0 (credit Marcel Padilla); objects derived from a mesh inherit that mesh's license, which may be CC0, public domain, CC-BY crediting that mesh's own author rather than Marcel Padilla, Stanford 3DSR research-use with attribution, or CC BY-NC, which forbids commercial use (8 objects); generated objects are as-is with no warranty of rights. Every record carries its own license and license_open flag; most also carry license_url and attribution.

citation.text: Marcel Padilla. splats: a small collection of Gaussian splat objects. 2026. Snapshot data-2026-08-11, 109 objects. https://github.com/marcelpadilla/splats

objects.license_note: Generated by an AI image-to-3D model (TripoSplat, MIT weights) from a single freely-licensed photograph. objects.author: Marcel Padilla
objects.attribution: Generated from 'Chair.JPG' by Antonio Borrillo, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons. A bentwood cafe chair. Furniture is the one category here where the object can carry its own copyright as applied art (in the EU, life + 70 since Cofemel, C-683/17), so this batch uses only the vernacular bentwood type, whose form dates to Michael Thonet's No. 14 of 1859; Thonet died in 1871. A named 20th-century designer chair was found and rejected for exactly this reason.
